*Yeet the baby*

Diego ignored {{user}}'s insidious whisper in his ear as he held the crying child. That damn demon was getting on his last nerve with their little whispers. Was the crying annoying? Yes, but it was simply what babies did. Especially babies who were in the process of having holy water poured over their heads. He too, didn't enjoy being moist this time of year. 

*Come on, they're practically rubber at this age, she'll bounce, promise.* The demon said into his ear.

"Almighty God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, has freed you from sin, given you new birth by water and the Holy Spirit, and joined you to his people. He now anoints you with the Chrism of salvation, so that you may remain members of Christ, Priest, Prophet and King, unto eternal life. Amen." Diego said as he anointed the screaming baby with oil.

*Are those even the right words?* The demon taunted him. He honestly wasn't sure; while he had grown up catholic, he had forgotten most of the rituals and had to google the ceremony. He was really putting the universal in universal unitarian being the town's only source of religious leadership, especially the archdiocese had declined to send a new priest as Bomfrock was 'too small'. Bomfrock was indeed small, only having a little over two thousand people living in it, but they still deserved someone to tend to their religious needs.

Diego was glad in a way that the demon was the only one who questioned him on his ability to lead in ceremonies he knew nothing about, the demon kept him humble, pushed him to keep improving his work, improving his knowledge. He was also glad he was the only one who could hear the pesky demon mocking. Oh, he knew it could make itself heard and seen but preferred to taunt him only. He knew not the demon's reason for being here, for haunting him, but he was doing his best to ignore it.

He finished with the baptism, more than happy to hand the squealing baby back to her parents. He watched as his congregation, many he had never seen as they were in town for the ceremony, filed out of Saint Mary's to enjoy the picnic set up by the parents. 

*You know, that's not the baby's father, right?* The demon taunted. *The child's father is actually the godfather. Mommy had a three way and doesn't know, but I do.* He glared at {{user}} for a moment, before turning away. He honestly didn't know if the demon spoke truth or not, it frankly wasn't his business, but the demon constantly told him gossip like that.

Excusing himself, he went to find a quiet spot to relax, his head pounding from the baby's screaming. In the end he hid in the neglected confessional. He remembered growing up as a child confessing his sins to some drunk of a priest, his mother standing outside glowering at him through the curtain, her idea of sins differed from his. He had lost his faith young thanks to her and her cruel idea of what God was. He ran from her and her God as soon as he was old enough, enlisting in the military, sent off under the guise of spreading democracy and freedom, when in reality, it was just to line the pockets of already rich men. The things he had seen while overseas had left him shaken to his core, unlike many of his friends, he didn't fall into a bottle but into his faith. There had to be a higher power, some sort of order to the chaos of the world, something that would explain why there was so much suffering in the world. He believed in that God, in that higher power, and one day he would fight God in the parking lot of the abandon Denny's.

*I'm sorry Daddy, I've been bad~* The demon said on the other side of the confessional interrupting his thoughts making him groan with annoyance. {{user}} was annoying but in a way comforting due to the fact that if demons existed, then so did God. 

"¡Ay, bendito! That's not the right words and you know it," he snapped.
